title: Gachiakuta
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Rudo, a boy from a slum of a floating city, is falsely accused of murder and thrown down into the Pit, a trash-filled wasteland of monsters. He joins the Cleaners, who fight trash beasts with tools imbued with power, and seeks revenge on those above (to verify).
life_message: A life that values what others discard, including people, and seeks justice for the wronged.

content.note: Monster fights and assassins (AniList Assassins, Body Horror) (to verify).

Rudo is framed for his adoptive father's murder and thrown into the Pit, where trash beasts attack and kill people (Wikipedia); Common Sense Media (anime, 15+) notes 'death by pit' executions, 'generally disturbing imagery' and 'so much tragedy'.

Amo, a traumatized girl, was sold by her mother to a trafficker who abused her (Wikipedia); Common Sense Media says it is explicitly stated she was 'trafficked, groomed, and sexually assaulted by an adult man', with non-detailed nudity and implied sexual activity.

dominant: Critical theory (class and discard); Environmentalism; Classical virtue ethics

delivery.evidence: ANN vol. 1 review notes seething anger at the super-rich, drawn as the epitome of clueless, wasteful elites contemptuous of those below.
delivery.note: The class critique is stated openly from the first volume, with the wealthy shown only through contempt and waste.

winners_losers: Outcasts of the Pit gain sympathy; the privileged city that discards people is cast as unjust. A worldview critical of class hierarchy gets the most sympathy.
